affordances.description: What creatures may DO with this object, declared so behaviors and interactions can target it by data: each entry names an action and the anchor it happens at (perch -> gallery; look_at -> lantern; shelter -> lee_side). An affordance is a contract, not code: the creature's behavior/interaction names the action, the scene resolves it to the placed instance's anchor.

anchors.description: Named points the rig reports per render, in GRID coords — the object's interface to the rest of the scene: effect sources (a lantern is where a beam/glow starts), interaction targets (a perch point), QA references. Other packages refer to anchors by name, never to object internals.

footprint.description: The object's extent in design units at scale 1, relative to the placement point, plus where it meets the medium (waterline_y offset) so the environment's causality table can ring/splash against it when a creature event happens at its base.

waterline_dy.description: Design-y offset from root_y of the surface line (0 = the placement point IS the waterline).

kind.description: Object class. landmark = a named, recognizable place-thing (Thomas Point Lighthouse); structure = generic built form (dock, bridge, blind); vegetation = a tree/cattail stand; vessel = a boat; furniture = small set dressing.

model_sheet.description: Package-relative path to the model sheet: canonical form, proportions, the real-world facts the drawing must keep.

palette.description: Named palette entries, same convention as species: index 0 is ALWAYS the canvas/background entry and must match the scene's background name so merged-palette compositing can share it. Object colors are the object's own — a landmark is drawn, in full, in its real colors (it is a thing in the world, not a caused mark; the environment's ink law does not apply to it).

module.description: Python module inside the package exposing the render contract.

render_fn.description: render(state, ctx) -> (uint8 index grid, {anchor_name: (x, y) in GRID coords}). Same contract as a species rig, with state in place of pose.

state_params.description: The object's animatable state — NOT a pose and NOT a behavior. Objects have no pacing, no life layer, and no learned dynamics: state is set by the scene (placement defaults), by the input bus/modes (lamp on at night), or by an interaction outcome (set_state). The rig renders deterministically from state every frame. root_x/root_y are the placement point in design coords (meaning defined per object, e.g. waterline centre); scale is scene-scale relative to design space.
